title: Jumpstart Kit: Rapid Instrumentation Guide for SDKs (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, action-oriented guide for instrumenting a Redwood SDK integration quickly so new integrators have useful telemetry and error visibility within their first 15–30 minutes.

Audience:
- SDK maintainers and integrators doing demo or first-prod wiring
- Solutions engineers running customer POCs

Goals (what this kit gets you in ~30 minutes):
- Baseline telemetry: request/response timing, success/error counts, token usage tag
- Minimal tracing: a single trace/span per API call with SDK version and route
- Lightweight local assertions: smoke checks that trigger concise logs for common failures
- Troubleshooting checklist to hand to support/SEs

Why this exists (short rationale):
Most early failures in SDK integrations are invisible: network glitches, credential misconfig, or silent latency regression. If we give a tiny, standardized instrumentation pattern, teams can triage POCs quickly and iterate on prompts without blind spots.

Quick architecture (1-line):
- Capture start/end timestamps around SDK calls, emit a compact event (JSON line) to local stdout or configured exporter; attach: sdk_name, sdk_version, model, route, status, tokens_consumed, client_id (if known).

Checklist (cut-and-paste):
- [ ] Add SDK_VERSION constant to top-level module
- [ ] Wrap outbound call in try/catch/finally and record start_ts/end_ts
- [ ] On success, emit: event_type=call_complete, duration_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, route
- [ ] On error, emit: event_type=call_error, error_type, http_code, error_message (trimmed), stack (optional)
- [ ] Attach trace_id correlation id from incoming request if available
- [ ] Gate verbose payload logging behind an env var (REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=true)

Minimal example (pseudo-code snippet to paste into an SDK entrypoint):

const SDK_VERSION = "0.3.1-nightly"
function callModel(payload, opts) {
  const start = Date.now()
  let success = false
  try {
    const resp = await http.post(url, buildReq(payload, opts))
    success = true
    return resp
  } catch (err) {
    emit({
      event_type: "call_error",
      sdk_version: SDK_VERSION,
      model: opts.model || "unknown",
      error_type: err.name || "Error",
      http_code: err.status || null,
      duration_ms: Date.now() - start
    })
    throw err
  } finally {
    if (success) emit({ event_type: "call_complete", sdk_version: SDK_VERSION, model: opts.model || "unknown", duration_ms: Date.now() - start })
  }
}

Emit format (single-line JSON recommendation):
- timestamp_iso, level (info|error), payload: { ...fields above... }
Example: 2025-02-02T15:12:03Z INFO {"event_type":"call_complete","sdk_version":"0.3.1-nightly","model":"redwood-v1","duration_ms":312} 

Local dev ergonomics:
- Default sink: stdout (so Platform/SE can capture logs in sandbox)
- Optional sink: OTLP/http exporter or local file for automated parsing in demos
- Keep event size small (<1KB) to avoid expensive logs in early POCs

Golden fields (always include):
- sdk_name, sdk_version, event_type, duration_ms, status (success|error), model, route, client_id (if known), request_id/trace_id

Support handoff checklist (for SEs/customer support):
- Ask for the last 10 call_complete/call_error lines (with timestamps)
- Confirm SDK_VERSION and model
- Check for repeated 5xx or auth errors within a 1-minute window
- If latency spikes, request a single trace (if tracing is enabled) or at minimum start/end timestamps for two consecutive failing calls

Known limitations and open questions (notes to self):
- We don't capture prompt length/token split automatically; need an SDK helper to estimate tokens locally (low priority).
- Privacy: make sure payload logging is gated and defaults to off for real product installs.
- Correlating with server-side Redwood logs: include route+request_id to make joins straightforward.
- Should we provide a tiny 'telemetry shim' NPM/PyPI package? (pros: copy-paste easy; cons: versioning overhead)

Integration scenarios (short):
- Demo hack: stdout sink + copy logs from sandbox session to support slack thread
- POC with customer: enable OTLP endpoint (temporary) and attach a simple Grafana dashboard with latency and error count
- Pre-prod: wire to customer telemetry with privacy redaction rules

Fast rollout plan (2 sprints):
- Sprint 1 (week 1): implement try/catch wrapper in JS + Python SDKs, add SDK_VERSION, and stdout emitter; ship as "instrumentation opt-in" feature flag
- Sprint 2 (week 2): publish telemetry shim (tiny package) and add demo dashboard templates + SE runbook

Templates to include in repo (short filenames):
- docs/telemetry/quick-emit-example.js
- docs/telemetry/quick-emit-example.py
- demos/sandbox/readme.md (how to collect logs)
- se/runbook/collect-logs-checklist.md

Example runbook snippet (for support):
- 1) Confirm SDK_VERSION in code or logs
- 2) Request last 10 events with timestamps
- 3) If errors, include the trimmed error_message and http_code
- 4) If latency, get call_complete duration_ms for 5 samples in a row

Unresolved items to decide in next sync:
- Minimal set of tag keys for PII-safe joins (e.g., client_id vs hashed_user_id)
- If we create telemetry-shim, what platforms (node/python/rs/go) to prioritize?

References and related artifacts:
- Confluence draft: SDK Telemetry Standards (link above)
- GH PR with initial wrapper: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482
- Slack thread: #devexp-onboarding (pin message id: 1352)

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep this guide intentionally tiny — the goal is "useful by default" not exhaustive.
- After we ship, collect SE feedback after 5 POCs and iterate on default fields.
- Demo flow idea: create a 7-step video showing log capture -> paste into ticket -> triage in 3 mins.

---
Document is intentionally informal — save as the compact kit in developer-experience repo and link from quickstart templates.
